content.value_statement: Architecture choices often outpace clear requirements and trade-off analysis. This skill structures discovery, pattern comparison, and decision records for explainable system designs.
actual_capabilities: Collects scale, team, timeline, domain, budget, legacy, compliance, and technology constraints before recommending an architecture.
Classifies projects as MVP, SaaS, or enterprise using documented scale, team, and timeline characteristics.
Compares data access, domain, distributed system, and API patterns using suitability and complexity guidance.
Produces architecture decision records covering context, options, rationale, trade-offs, consequences, mitigation, and revisit triggers.
Identifies premature complexity and suggests simpler alternatives for microservices, CQRS, event sourcing, repositories, and layered architectures.
limitations: Does not inspect repositories, infrastructure, runtime metrics, or production environments automatically.
Provides general pattern guidance that requires validation against the specific domain and operational constraints.
Does not implement, deploy, benchmark, or test the recommended architecture.
Examples use broad project categories and may not represent unusual compliance, availability, or data residency requirements.

use_cases.title: Shape an MVP Architecture
use_cases.description: Select a simple starting architecture and define measurable conditions for adding complexity later.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a SaaS Design
use_cases.description: Compare modular, data access, and communication patterns against team size, product domains, and growth expectations.
use_cases.target_user: Technical leads and product engineering teams

use_cases.title: Document Enterprise Decisions
use_cases.description: Create decision records that expose rationale, accepted risks, mitigations, and future review conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a New System
prompt_templates.prompt: Ask me the context questions needed to design [system]. Cover scale, team, timeline, domain, constraints, and missing success criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before selecting any architecture or pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Architecture Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [patterns] for [system]. Use requirements [requirements] and constraints [constraints]. Show benefits, costs, complexity, validity conditions, and a recommendation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when several patterns appear viable.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Architecture Decision Record
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an architecture decision record for [decision]. Include context, options, rationale, accepted trade-offs, consequences, mitigations, and revisit triggers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use to document a significant technical choice.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Architecture Evolution
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an architecture for [system] at [scale]. Explain component choices, rejected alternatives, operational consequences, and measurable triggers for revisiting each major decision.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a complete design with an evolution path.

output_examples.input: Choose an architecture for a solo-developed commerce MVP serving fewer than 1,000 users.
output: Recommendation: Use a monolith with PostgreSQL and direct ORM access.
Rationale: The small team, short timeline, and transactional orders favor simplicity and ACID guarantees.
Revisit when usage exceeds 10,000 users or team ownership requires independent services.

output_examples.input: Compare a modular monolith with microservices for a six-person SaaS team.
output: Choose a modular monolith because the team can maintain clear domain boundaries without distributed operations.
Microservices offer independent scaling but add deployment, observability, consistency, and coordination costs.
Revisit if teams grow beyond ten developers or individual domains require different scaling.

output_examples.input: Document the decision to introduce a repository layer for a complex billing domain.
output: Decision: Introduce repositories around billing aggregates to isolate persistence and support focused testing.
Accepted trade-off: Additional interfaces and mapping increase implementation complexity.
Revisit if the domain becomes simple CRUD or the abstraction stops supporting multiple persistence needs.

best_practices: Gather measurable requirements and constraints before recommending patterns.
Tie every decision to a specific problem, rejected alternatives, and accepted consequences.
Define objective triggers for revisiting decisions as scale, team structure, or domain complexity changes.
anti_patterns: Do not choose microservices solely for possible future scale.
Do not add repositories, CQRS, or event sourcing without a concrete problem they solve.
Do not treat generic examples as validated production designs.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide expected users, data volume, transaction rate, team size, timeline, domain complexity, budget, compliance needs, and current technology constraints.

faq.question: Can this skill choose between a monolith and microservices?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares scaling needs, domain boundaries, team size, and operational complexity before recommending an option.

faq.question: Does this skill create architecture decision records?
faq.answer: Yes. It structures context, options, decisions, rationale, trade-offs, consequences, mitigations, and revisit triggers.

faq.question: Will this skill inspect my codebase?
faq.answer: No. It depends on the project information you provide and does not automatically inspect files, infrastructure, or runtime behavior.

faq.question: Does it support event-driven architecture decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. It evaluates real-time needs, loose coupling, message queues, and tolerance for eventual consistency.

faq.question: Can I use the recommendation without further review?
faq.answer: No. Validate recommendations through domain review, security assessment, testing, operational analysis, and environment-specific evidence.
